result.title: Cascade Family Health — Printing
result.body: Print queues are hosted on the CASC-SRV-01 print server. Users are mapped by department via Group Policy. The most common failure is a stuck spooler after a driver update; clearing the queue and restarting the Print Spooler service resolves the majority of reports.

result.title: Runbook — Account lockout and root cause
result.body: Unlock the account, then find the cause. Repeated lockouts are almost always a stale credential cached on a device: a mapped drive, a saved Wi-Fi profile, a service running as the user, or a phone with an old mail password. Check recent sign-in failures by source device before closing. Closing an unlock without a root-cause check produces a repeat ticket within days and is counted as a failed resolution.

result.title: Cascade Family Health — Network and VPN
result.body: Cascade Family Health uses a pre-shared key VPN profile pushed through Intune. Split tunnelling is disabled. Remote users must be members of the "VPN Users" security group before the profile will authenticate. Business hours are 7:00 to 19:00. The weekly maintenance window is day 0 at 1:00 for 5 hours.

outcome.internalNote:
CASC-SRV-01 (file shares, print, LOB DB host) unreachable via ICMP/agent for 12+ min, coinciding with start of the Sun 01:00 5hr maintenance window.

What I checked:
- getDevice(CASC-SRV-01) returned null — device is unreachable to remote tooling entirely (no OS/patch/software data retrievable), consistent with the host being down or the agent offline, not just a service issue.
- getMaintenanceWindow confirms window is day 0, 01:00, 5hrs — alert onset lines up with window start, so this could be a maintenance reboot that hasn't come back, but could equally be a genuine unplanned outage that happens to coincide. Cannot distinguish remotely.
- searchDocumentation found only the print-spooler/stuck-queue runbook and account lockout runbook — nothing specific to this server's maintenance job or reboot schedule, so I cannot confirm whether a reboot was actually scheduled/executed on this host tonight or what patch/update was being applied.

Why it stopped here: getDevice returning null means there is no remote read/write path to this host — Runbook 12 (service restart with dependency awareness) is not applicable because I cannot even read device/service state, let alone verify a restart. This matches the triage note: needs a technician with console/out-of-band (iDRAC/iLO) or on-site access to check power/boot state, confirm whether POST completed, whether it's hung at a BIOS/update screen, or genuinely powered off/networking down.

Recommended next step: Technician should use iDRAC/iLO (or on-site access) to check power state and console output. If mid-boot/hung, force a clean reboot and watch POST. If the maintenance job triggered a patch/firmware update that didn't complete, may need to resume/rollback via console before services (file share, print spooler, LOB DB) are restarted — restart those in dependency order (DB before app-layer/file shares/print) only once the host itself is confirmed up, per Runbook 12 step 3. This is a P1 single-server outage affecting the whole site.
